name: dogd

properties.global: Every device that boots this URL mounts the identical filesystem.
properties.addressable: Every node has a real URL. `open /learnwithkody/examples/` goes somewhere.
properties.versioned: It is a git tree. Every change to the filesystem has an author and a diff.
properties.no-server: There is no API server. The API is files.
properties.read-only: Not a policy, a fact: a browser cannot write to someone else's Pages site.

why-read-only-matters: A global writable layer would need accounts, auth, quotas, moderation and a server. Making the global layer read-only is what lets the whole OS be static. Writes are a local concern, so they go to a local device.
